data.about: Two beams that have to carry a load and let pipes, a window and a door through at the same time. Both are double cantilevers, and their supports are set far enough in that sagging disappears completely — work it out and the whole length turns out to be hogging, so the TENSION chord is the top one everywhere. Which is exactly where every one of the openings has been cut. The flow has to detour under them, and the detour costs depth. No load value is printed, so drag it and watch the picture stay the same: this one is about geometry, not numbers.

data.name: lcost
data.text: routed under the openings: lever arm 1.26 m instead of 2.00 m, chord force +59 %

steps.caption: EX 7 task 3: two beams with holes cut through them for pipes, a window and a door. Find a force flow that gets round them
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: a beam ten metres long and two deep on two INTERIOR supports, so it cantilevers at both ends. The sheet prints no load value — this is a qualitative task, so drag the load and watch nothing about the picture change
steps.title: What is given

steps.caption: a double cantilever usually does both — hogging over the supports and sagging between them. Work it out here and something better turns up
steps.title: Where it sags and where it hogs

steps.caption: blue is the compression path and pink the tension it pulls against. Drawn without regard for the openings first, so you can see exactly which ones are in the way
steps.title: The natural force flow

steps.caption: the tie cannot run through a hole, so it drops below the lowest row of them and comes back up. It costs lever arm, so the force in that stretch goes up — that is the price of the pipes
steps.title: Routing round the openings

steps.caption: switch to the right-hand beam. Its window sits in the left cantilever and its door beyond the roller — both in hogging zones, both near the TOP. A hole is cheap where the chord it interrupts is lightly loaded, and expensive where it is not
steps.title: Where you may cut a hole
